To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HPV changes are more common in multifocal disease and in younger patients, that HPV-associated multifocal disease is not associated with nodal metastases, and that HPV-associated multifocality may represent a distinct clinicopathologic entity.
HPV-associated multifocal vulvar cancers occur in younger patients and do not have lymph node metastasis.
the presence of HPV changes in patients with invasive cancer of the vulva is associated with a lower age group and with a multifocal distribution of the lesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinicopathologic features associated with HPV infection of the vulva.
the clinicopathologic features of invasive squamous cell cancer of the vulva in patients with associated HPV changes.
the association between HPV changes and invasive squamous cell cancer of the vulva, and with the age and nodal metastasis in these patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HPV changes in the vulvar epithelium are not associated with an increased risk of nodal metastases in patients with invasive vulvar cancer.
the presence of HPV changes in patients with invasive cancer of the vulva is associated with a younger mean age, a multifocal distribution, and an absence of nodal metastases.
multifocal invasive vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with HPV changes has no nodal metastases, while unifocal invasive vulvar cancer with or without HPV changes is more likely to have nodal disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV-related changes are more likely to be present in younger women with invasive squamous cancer, and multifocal disease is associated with HPV-related changes.
the presence of multifocal lesions and HPV changes are associated with a younger age group and a decreased incidence of nodal spread.
the presence of HPV changes in patients with vulvar cancer correlates with a younger age, unifocal disease, and lack of nodal metastases in patients with invasive carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incidence of HPV-related lesions of the vulva is higher among younger women.
HPV-associated vulvar cancers are more likely to be multifocal and to have a lower risk of metastasis.
the presence of HPV changes is associated with multifocal disease in patients with invasive vulvar cancer.
